claims.text: The starting material is a homogeneous CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix without secondary phases.
Approximately 5 vol% h-BN nanoparticles can be uniformly dispersed throughout the CoCrFeNi matrix during processing.
Adding 5 vol% h-BN nanoparticles will promote an in situ tribo-layer containing h-BN and wear debris.
The h-BN-containing tribo-layer will remain stable at high temperatures up to 800 °C.
h-BN nanoparticles reduce local shear strength during sliding.
A persistent h-BN-containing lubricious film mitigates frictional forces.
A persistent h-BN-containing lubricious film protects the alloy against wear.
The proposed lubricating mechanism will continue to operate despite temperature-induced oxidative changes in the matrix.
Relative to undoped CoCrFeNi, the h-BN-doped alloy will have a significantly lower coefficient of friction across the full range from room temperature to 800 °C.
Relative to undoped CoCrFeNi, the h-BN-doped alloy will have a lower wear rate across the full range from room temperature to 800 °C.
Undoped CoCrFeNi exhibits increasing coefficient of friction as temperature rises.
Undoped CoCrFeNi exhibits increasing wear as temperature rises.
The temperature-dependent deterioration of undoped CoCrFeNi is caused by unstable tribo-film formation and oxidation effects.
The proposed performance scope is sliding in ambient air from room temperature to 800 °C under a load of approximately 50 N.
